title: Cohen–Macaulay loci and arbitrary field extension
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a locally finite-type $k$-scheme, and $K/k$ any field extension. Write $p:X_K=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ for the projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. A point $x'\in X_K$ with image $x$ belongs to the Cohen–Macaulay locus of $X_K$ if and only if $x$ belongs to the Cohen–Macaulay locus of $X$. Here Cohen–Macaulay at a point means that the depth of the Noetherian local ring equals its Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-depth], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

Consequently, if $f:X\to S$ is a locally finite-type morphism of Noetherian schemes, the relative Cohen–Macaulay locus $U_f$, consisting of points $x$ at which the local ring of the ordinary fibre $X_{f(x)}$ is Cohen–Macaulay, is also the locus obtained by testing geometric fibres. For any base change $S'\to S$ with $S'$ Noetherian, the relative Cohen–Macaulay locus of $f':X\times_SS'\to S'$ is the inverse image of $U_f$. No perfectness of the residue fields and no separability or finite-generation assumption on $K/k$ is required.

Here a Noetherian scheme admits a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings, and a ring is Noetherian when every ideal is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

source.place: Stacks Tags 00RJ (Cohen–Macaulay locus after an arbitrary field extension, lemma-extend-field-CM-locus) and 00RK (relative Cohen–Macaulay locus commutes with base change, lemma-CM-locus-commutes-base-change).

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ and $x'\in X_K$ above it. Choose an affine finite-type $k$-neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $x$, using the definition of locally finite type. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$; hence the finite-type algebra $B$ is finitely presented. Every $k$-module is flat, so $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat by the affine flatness equivalence, and it is locally finitely presented by its finite presentation. Apply the quasi-finite polynomial chart theorem to obtain an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq V$ containing $x$, an integer $n$, and a locally finitely presented locally quasi-finite map $e:U\to\mathbb A^n_k$, with $n=\dim_xV$. Restriction to an open neighbourhood does not change dimension at the point: intersections with that open are a cofinal family of neighbourhoods. Thus $n=\dim_xU$. The stalks at $x$ in $X,V,U$ coincide, by the germ description of stalks.

source.place: Tag 00RJ, first reduction; Tag 00QE (lemma-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra), a quasi-finite polynomial chart suffices in place of the finite normalization chart of Tag 00OZ.

proof.text: Write $A=k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, so $\mathbb A^n_k=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The chart $e$ is induced by a map $A\to C$. Its finite presentation on affine opens implies $C=A[z_1,\ldots,z_r]/(h_1,\ldots,h_m)$ for finitely many polynomials; in particular $C$ is a finite-type $k$-algebra, generated by the images of the $t_i,z_j$. The same presentation exhibits $C$ as a finitely presented $k$-algebra, so $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite presentation. It is flat because the $k$-module $C$ is flat and the affine flatness equivalence applies. Set $A_K=A\otimes_kK=K[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ and $C_K=C\otimes_kK$. The affine fibre-product theorem identifies $U_K$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C_K$ and identifies the base-changed chart with $\operatorname{Spec}(A_K\to C_K)$. Indeed $C\otimes_A A_K\simeq C_K$ sends $c\otimes(a\otimes\lambda)$ to $ca\otimes\lambda$, with inverse $c\otimes\lambda\mapsto c\otimes(1\otimes\lambda)$. The polynomial identification sends $t^I\otimes\lambda$ to $\lambda t^I$ and its inverse sends $\sum_I\lambda_I t^I$ to $\sum_I t^I\otimes\lambda_I$. Let $\mathfrak q,\mathfrak q_K$ be the primes representing $x,x'$ and let $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak p_K$ be their contractions to $A,A_K$. Affine stalks are their prime localizations.

source.place: Tag 00RJ (lemma-extend-field-CM-locus), displayed local-ring square; affine base change by Schemes Tags 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes) and 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines).

proof.text: The base-changed chart $e_K:U_K\to\mathbb A^n_K$ is locally quasi-finite and locally finitely presented by stability of these properties under base change. Its structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is flat, since every $K$-module is flat and flatness of affine morphisms is equivalent to ring flatness. It is locally finitely presented: tensoring the displayed finite presentation of $C$ gives $C_K=K[t_1,\ldots,t_n,z_1,\ldots,z_r]/(h_{1,K},\ldots,h_{m,K})$, with exactly the same finite sets of generators and equations. By invariance of dimension at a point under field extension, $\dim_{x'}U_K=\dim_xU=n$. This is topological dimension at a point, not the dimension of the local ring.

source.place: Tag 00RJ, dimension comparison using Tag 00P4; Morphisms Tags 01TM and 01TS.

proof.text: Apply the polynomial-chart fibre-flat criterion first over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to $U$ and then over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ to $U_K$. Their fibres over the unique base points are $U$ and $U_K$ themselves. The dimension equalities just proved remove the dimension clause of that criterion. Consequently $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if $C_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $A_{\mathfrak p}$; and $\mathcal O_{X_K,x'}$ is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if $(C_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ is flat over $(A_K)_{\mathfrak p_K}$. All hypotheses of the criterion are in force: affine bases, affine sources, flat locally finitely presented structure morphisms, and locally quasi-finite locally finitely presented charts.

source.place: Tag 00RJ, use of Tag 00RE (lemma-where-CM); here its existing scheme-level formulation is applied to both charts.

proof.text: For ascent of chart flatness, suppose $C_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $A_{\mathfrak p}$. It is flat over $A$ by the equivalence for modules over a localization. Apply localized module base change to the tensor square $A\to C$, $A_K\to C_K$, with $N=C$ and $M=C_K$; the comparison $C_K\otimes_C C\simeq C_K$ is multiplication with inverse $c'\mapsto c'\otimes1$. It follows that $(C_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ is flat over $A_K$. The same localization equivalence makes it flat over $(A_K)_{\mathfrak p_K}$.

source.place: Tag 00RJ, ascent part of Tag 00MQ (lemma-base-change-flat-up-down); Tag 00HT (2).

proof.text: For descent, both $A\to A_K$ and $C\to C_K$ are faithfully flat by field-extension base change, hence flat. Localizing these maps at the indicated primes gives flat local maps $A_{\mathfrak p}\to(A_K)_{\mathfrak p_K}$ and $C_{\mathfrak q}\to(C_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$. The latter is faithfully flat because it is flat and local. If $(C_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ is flat over $(A_K)_{\mathfrak p_K}$, composition shows it is flat over $A_{\mathfrak p}$. Apply faithful-flat descent to $A_{\mathfrak p}\to C_{\mathfrak q}\to(C_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$: the last ring is faithfully flat over the middle ring and flat over the first. Thus $C_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $A_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Tag 00RJ, descent part of Tag 00MQ; Tags 00HR and 039V.

proof.text: Combining the two flatness implications with the two Cohen–Macaulay equivalences proves the pointwise assertion for $x,x'$. Every such pair is covered by the chosen affine neighbourhood and its inverse image; restricting to these opens preserves their local rings by restriction of germs. Thus the Cohen–Macaulay locus upstairs is exactly the inverse image of the locus downstairs, for arbitrary $K/k$. No part of the argument used separability, perfectness, or finite generation of the extension.

For the relative assertion, let $s=f(x)$ and identify the ordinary fibre $X_s$ with its subspace of $X$. On an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ around $x,s$, its ring is $B\otimes_R\kappa(s)$; if $B$ is generated by finitely many elements over $R$, their tensors generate this fibre algebra over $\kappa(s)$. Hence $X_s$ is locally of finite type over $\kappa(s)$, as required by the result already proved. By the definition of geometric fibre, $X_{\bar s}=X_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\overline{\kappa(s)}$. The pointwise result says that at every lift of $x$ its local ring is Cohen–Macaulay exactly when $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ is. There is at least one such lift: on a finite-type affine neighbourhood of $x$ in $X_s$, field-extension base change is faithfully flat and therefore surjective on spectra. Thus testing any, or every, geometric lift gives the same locus $U_f$.

Now let $g:S'\to S$ be the specified base change and $x'\in X'=X\times_SS'$. Write $s'=f'(x')$, $s=g(s')$, and $x=p(x')$. The induced residue-field map makes $\kappa(s')$ a field extension of $\kappa(s)$. The universal property of fibre products gives $X'_{s'}\simeq X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')$, compatibly with the images $x',x$: a map into either side is exactly a map to $X$, a map to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')$, and equality of their composites to $S$; composing the second map with $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ supplies the intermediate fibre factor. Apply the pointwise assertion to the locally finite-type $\kappa(s)$-scheme $X_s$ and this field extension. It gives $\mathcal O_{X'_{s'},x'}$ Cohen–Macaulay if and only if $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ is. These are exactly $x'\in U_{f'}$ and $p(x')\in U_f$, so $U_{f'}=p^{-1}(U_f)$.
